Performers
Sergei Rachmaninoff (piano) Documented[1] [4]
Work version
Solo piano, performed by the composer Documented

No performing score edition is identified.

[1] [4]
Recorded
1919-04-24 Documented

The earlier Commons file gives 24 April 1919. The primary National Park Service catalogue confirms only the year 1919; December 1920 is the release date.

[3] [4]
Place
New York City Documented

City given by the earlier Commons description; no studio is identified. The National Park Service entry does not supply a venue.

[3]
Label
Edison Records — Diamond Disc Documented[1] [4]
Catalogue
82187-R Documented

Released December 1920. The transferred museum object is NPS EDIS 73898; that museum number is not the commercial catalogue number.

[1] [4]
Matrix, take, sides
Matrix 6742-C-2-3 [2-1]; side R of Edison Diamond Disc 82187 Documented

The complete matrix string is transcribed as printed by the National Park Service; its suffixes are not independently decoded into take or pressing information.

[1] [4]
Transfer
Adam Cuerden — cleanup and restoration; source audio published by the United States National Park Service Documented

The National Park Service supplies the source disc identification and audio file. It does not name the original transfer engineer.

[1] [3] [4]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

No original transfer or restoration date is stated. The National Park Service page update (2004), earlier Commons upload (2007), Adam Cuerden’s original upload (2009) and Commons import (2014) are not treated as transfer dates.

[1] [3] [4]
Processing
Cleaned and restored copy of the earlier Commons file Prelude 3 2 Rach playing.ogg Documented

Commons credits Adam Cuerden, but gives no restoration settings or speed-correction log. No aural comparison has been made.

[1] [3]
Composition rights
Public domain under the Commons notice for an author who died in 1943 Documented

The notice scopes its life-term assertion to countries with life plus 80 years or fewer. This concerns Rachmaninoff’s composition, not an assertion that any modern edition is unrestricted.

[1]
Recording rights
Rule 2 — sound recording public domain in the United States (first published by 1925). Documented

Commons applies PD-old-auto-record-expired and identifies Edison Diamond Disc 82187-R, matrix 6742-C-2-3 [2-1]. The opened National Park Service catalogue independently distinguishes the 1919 recording from its December 1920 release. December 1920 is before the programme’s 1925 US first-publication cutoff; this is a sound-recording term, not merely the composition’s status.

[5] [6] [7]

Sergei Rachmaninoff: Prelude in C♯ minor, Op. 3 No. 2, played by the composer (1919). Edison Diamond Disc 82187-R, matrix 6742-C-2-3 [2-1], NPS EDIS 73898. National Park Service source audio; cleanup and restoration by Adam Cuerden; via Wikimedia Commons. Public-domain recording in the United States. Rights statement
